---
title: "Data"
---

Source files and analysis outputs are about 185 GB and are kept outside the
repository. The code reaches them through a single setting, `DATA_ROOT`.

## Pointing the code at a data folder

Resolution order, first match wins:

1. environment variable `MS_FORESTS_VPD_DATA`
2. key `DATA_ROOT` in `config/settings.local.yaml`, which is not under version control
3. key `DATA_ROOT` in `config/settings.yaml`, the default committed value

Setting the environment variable is the least intrusive option:

```bash
# Windows PowerShell
$env:MS_FORESTS_VPD_DATA = "D:/ms-forests-vpd-data"

# macOS / Linux
export MS_FORESTS_VPD_DATA=/data/ms-forests-vpd-data
```

Or create `config/settings.local.yaml`:

```yaml
DATA_ROOT: D:/ms-forests-vpd-data
```

Everything else in `config/settings.yaml` is a path relative to `DATA_ROOT` and is
resolved by `src/paths.py`. If the folder cannot be found, `src.paths` raises on import
with a message naming the environment variable.

## Folder layout

```
<DATA_ROOT>/
└── data/
    ├── 00_raw/
    │   ├── ameriflux/
    │   ├── fluxnet_from_carbonportal/
    │   ├── fluxnet_from_fluxnetorg/
    │   ├── from-fluxnet-shuttle/
    │   └── japanflux/
    └── outputs/
        ├── 10_datasets/
        ├── 20_subsets/
        ├── 30_shap/
        ├── 40_aggregation/
        ├── 50_plots/
        └── 80_info/
```

Each `00_raw/<source>/` folder holds the unpacked site archives of that source plus a
`0-info/` subfolder with the site metadata file. Folder and file name patterns per
source are in `config/settings.yaml`.

The Natural Earth country outlines used by Figure 1 are small enough to ship with the
code and live in the repository under `data/worldmap/`.

## Source datasets

Half-hourly FLUXNET-formatted files from five sources. Where a site appears in more
than one source, the higher-priority dataset wins and the others are used to extend the
record backwards (see `src/files.py::create_parquet_files`).

| Source | Access |
|--------|--------|
| FLUXNET-SHUTTLE | <https://fluxnet.org/> |
| FLUXNET2015 (ICOS Carbon Portal) | <https://www.icos-cp.eu/> |
| FLUXNET2015 (fluxnet.org) | <https://fluxnet.org/data/fluxnet2015-dataset/> |
| AmeriFlux FLUXNET | <https://ameriflux.lbl.gov/> |
| JapanFlux2024 | <https://www.japanflux.org/> |

All five require registration and carry their own data policies, so the raw files
cannot be redistributed here.

## Which outputs are needed for which step

Most steps read the output of the previous one. Two shortcuts are worth knowing:

- Everything from `30_shap` onwards runs from `outputs/20_subsets/`, which holds one
  small parquet file per site. Rebuilding those from raw is only necessary if the site
  selection or the filtering changes.
- The figure scripts read `outputs/40_aggregation/` and `outputs/30_shap/` and do not
  retrain any model.

## ERA5 credentials

Only needed for scripts `16a` to `16d`.

**Google Earth Engine** (`16a`, `16b`): a Google account registered for Earth Engine and
a cloud project. Authenticate once with `earthengine authenticate`. Earth Engine applies
rate limits, so start with two to four parallel batches.

**Copernicus Climate Data Store** (`16c`, `16d`): a CDS account and an API key in
`~/.cdsapirc`. Requests are queued server-side and can take hours. Some sites come back
empty or all-zero, which script `17` detects and rejects.

Both are optional. `17_add_era5_info.py` merges whatever is present and falls back
between sources, see [Methods](methods.qmd#era5-climate-normals).
